entities.name: Mithridates I of Pontus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Mithridates I Ctistes, also known as Mithridates III of Cius, was a Persian nobleman and the founder of the Kingdom of Pontus in Anatolia.

Born around 300 BCE to a minor noble family in the region of Cilicia, Mithridates rose to prominence through his military prowess and strategic alliances. He became king of Pontus at the age of 50 following the death of his predecessor and went on to expand his kingdom through conquests and shrewd diplomacy.

In 265 BCE, Mithridates I died without an heir, marking the beginning of a new era in Pontic history as his successors would face challenges from neighboring powers and internal conflicts. His legacy would shape the region for centuries to come, with his descendants playing key roles in regional politics and trade.

Mithridates' reign also saw significant cultural developments, including the spread of Greek language and art throughout Pontus, which had a lasting impact on the region's identity.

The tomb of Mithridates I was discovered in 1970 near the city of Sinop, featuring intricate carvings that depict his military campaigns and royal attire. The site has been recognized as a significant archaeological find and a testament to the enduring legacy of this enigmatic figure.
